_comment: Cents per point. cash = 1.0 by definition. These are DEFAULTS and are opinions, not facts. User-overridable in Options.
_sources: Added 2026-09-27. wf and bofa are the issuers' own fixed values: Wells Fargo prices a point at one cent on the Autograph page, and BofA Travel Rewards points redeem at one cent against travel and dining. The airline and hotel currencies are NerdWallet's September 2026 estimates (nerdwallet.com/travel/learn/airline-miles-and-hotel-points-valuations, updated 2026-09-14; hyatt, ihg and jetblue added 2026-09-28 from the same table, and wyndham and emirates after them), which price a typical award redemption rather than the best one. usaa is the issuer's own figure: the Eagle Navigator terms price 10,000 points at $100 in travel ($70 as cash). bilt is the same NerdWallet page's baseline for Bilt Rewards, 1.25 cents, rather than its 1.8-cent transfer estimate, because the defaults assume a booking through the issuer's own travel portal. ulta is the floor of Ulta Beauty's own redemption scale, 100 points = $3.00; larger redemptions are worth up to 6.25 cents (2,000 points = $125). usbank is U.S. Bank's own figure since 2026-09-29: the rewards calculators on the Altitude Go, Altitude Connect and Business Altitude Connect pages (cardrewards.usbank.com) price a point at a cent -- '1 point = $.01' -- redeemed for travel or as a deposit to a U.S. Bank account, and each Altitude card's caution says so; until then it was an assumption. frontier and milesandmore are not in NerdWallet's table, so each is the lowest September 2026 figure found, in keeping with a typical redemption rather than the best: frontier is WalletHub's average, 0.98 cents (wallethub.com, 2026-09-15; Upgraded Points says 1.1 and The Points Guy 1.3), and milesandmore is One Mile at a Time's 1.2 cents (onemileatatime.com/guides/value-miles-points, 2026-09-02; Upgraded Points says 1.3). carnival follows the same rule: no Carnival page states what a Carnival Rewards point is worth, so it is WalletHub's average, 0.92 cents (wallethub.com, 2026-09-15; The Points Guy's launch review put sample redemptions at 1 to 2 cents). gm is General Motors' own figure, $0.01 a point redeemed through GM (experience.gm.com/rewards/redeem); it is a currency of its own rather than cash because the points spend only with GM. breeze is Barclays' own figure: the Breeze Easy Visa page prices 30,000 BreezePoints at $300 of award travel. gmbusiness is GM's own figure too: GM Business Card Points are not GM Rewards points and redeem only at GM dealers, and GM's support page (experience.gm.com/support/account/rewards/business-card) converted the old Marcus card's Earnings at 100 points per $1. kroger is Kroger's own figure: 100 Kroger Points = $1 off groceries (kroger.com/pr/points-program, read 2026-09-29); the same 100 points take 10 cents a gallon off at a Kroger fuel center, on up to 35 gallons, so a large fill-up is worth up to 3.5 cents a point. royalone is BofA's own figure: the Royal ONE pages price their bonus points at a cent in onboard credit or cruise discounts (30,000 for $300), the only redemptions. ncl is Norwegian's own figure: the WorldPoints table on ncl.com/world-points prices every onboard-credit and cruise-discount reward at a cent a point (10,000 = $100). princess and hal are Barclays' own figure: the Princess and Holland America cards' terms redeem points at 1% as statement credits against the line's own, its sister lines' or airline charges of $50 or more. All four read 2026-09-30.
